concerns.text: T011b requires executing a power analysis to determine 'required_iterations' before T017 can generate 'data/sweep/params.csv'. However, T011b's description implies it needs simulation parameters (n, p, rho) to run the analysis, which are only defined in T017. This creates a circular dependency (T017 needs T011b output; T011b needs T017 parameters) making the task sequence unexecutable as written.

T019 describes a 'streaming data generator' that yields arrays to a 'downstream callback function'. The task does not define the callback's interface, signature, or the specific downstream consumer that will receive these yields. An implementer cannot execute this task without inventing the callback contract, violating self-containment.

T022 requires regenerating data 'on-the-fly' using seeds from 'data/sweep/seed_map.json' to run tests. However, the task does not specify the exact algorithm to map a seed to a specific (n, p, rho) configuration or how to handle the 'p/n > 10' check if the regenerated data violates FR-009. The logic for 'regenerating' is assumed but not detailed enough for deterministic execution.

T028 mandates using the 'exact same seed sequence as T022' for the permutation test. It does not specify how to reset the RNG state to match T022's state at the exact point of permutation, nor does it define the permutation algorithm (e.g., shuffling rows vs columns) required to 'respect the correlation structure'. Without this, the 'Gold Standard' cannot be deterministically reproduced.

T042 asks to generate a 'Failure Visualization' for the 'worst-case scenario'. The task does not define how to programmatically identify the 'worst-case' (e.g., max KS, max rho, or specific p/n ratio) from the available data. The implementer must guess the selection criteria, making the task non-deterministic.

T044 requires a 'Reality Check' composite plot overlaying three distributions. The task does not specify the exact data sources for the 'observed p-value distribution' (which seed/iteration?) or the 'permutation-based Gold Standard' (which specific run?). It assumes the implementer knows which specific artifacts to pull, lacking self-containment.

T040 requires extracting the 'worst-case' scenario from 'sensitivity.csv' to update documentation. Similar to T042, it fails to define the sorting or filtering logic to identify the 'worst-case' row (e.g., highest KS, highest rho, or specific p/n). The task is ambiguous on the selection criteria.
